title: J.X: Partly for Invariata-only party — do not cling to early wording into papal species-presence sense; Naumburg 1561 preface warned
pass_a_gloss: Partly for the favor of the Invariata Confession in particular, and of those who embrace this alone and with the oppression and extermination of the Variata, lest, while they strive too superstitiously to cling to the words of the earlier one, they be driven to the pontifical phrase concerning the presence of the Body and Blood of Christ in the Supper under the species of bread and wine, and to the sense of this phrase uniquely received in the Western Church at the time when the Confession was published — which the Estates of the Empire gathered at Naumburg in the year 61 already long ago hinted was to be feared, in their preface prefixed to the Invariata Augsburg Confession and addressed to Emperor Ferdinand;
pass_b_english: Partly it was for the Invariata in particular — and for those who hug that form alone while crushing and wiping out the Variata.

If they cling too superstitiously to the earlier wording, they can be pushed into the papal phrase about Christ's Body and Blood present in the Supper under the species of bread and wine, in the sense the Western Church alone then held when the Confession was issued.
The Imperial Estates at Naumburg in 1561 already flagged that danger in the preface they set before the Invariata and addressed to Emperor Ferdinand.
source_text: Partim in gratiam Invariatae Confessionis in specie, hancque solam & cum oppressione ac exterminio Variatae, amplectentium, ne, dum nimis superstitiose verbis prioris inhaerere satagunt, ad phrasin Pontificiam de praesentia Corporis & Sanguinis Christi in Coena sub Speciebus panis & vini, hujusque phraseos sensum, eo tempore, quo Confessio edebatur, Occidentali Ecclesiae unice receptum, adigantur, id quod metuendum fuisse jam olim innuere Status Imperii, Naunburgi Anno 61. congregati, in praefatione sua, Augustanae Confessioni Invariatae praemissa & Ferdinando Imperatori inscripta;
